title: Regional migration of a SaaS transactional data platform
description: A business-to-business SaaS provider runs its main transactional platform on a single self-managed PostgreSQL cluster in an EU data center. The platform serves customers in the EU and the United Kingdom, processes sustained write traffic, and has experienced two storage-related incidents in the last year. The organization must choose a migration strategy that improves resilience without causing a risky all-at-once rewrite.
objective: Select a three-year database and deployment architecture that improves recovery capability, preserves regulatory boundaries, and can be introduced incrementally within the available team and budget.
constraints: No planned migration event may interrupt writes for more than 5 minutes.
EU customer records must remain stored and backed up within the EU.
The target recovery point objective is at most 5 minutes.
The target recovery time objective is at most 30 minutes.
First-year infrastructure and migration spending may increase by no more than 25 percent over the current annual platform cost.
Eight platform engineers must continue supporting normal product delivery during the migration.
A tested rollback path must remain available until each migration phase is accepted.
The first migration phase cannot require customer-facing API or tenant-schema changes.
Security and administrative audit records must remain queryable for seven years.
The first production resilience improvement must be delivered within six months.
context: The primary database contains approximately 9 TB and grows by about 180 GB per month.
Peak traffic reaches approximately 12000 writes per second for short periods.
The application is a modular monolith with 46 tenant-aware schemas and several cross-schema transactions.
A recent logical-replication test sustained 70 percent of observed peak write traffic before replication lag increased continuously.
Current backups are encrypted and copied to a second EU facility, but restoration of the full dataset has not been rehearsed in the last 12 months.
The team has strong PostgreSQL operational experience but limited production experience with sharding.
Candidate directions include a managed regional PostgreSQL service, a self-managed dual-site design, and gradual extraction of high-volume workloads into separate data stores.
Contractual requirements for UK customer data after a regional disaster have not yet been consolidated into one approved rule.
stated_facts: The current production database is a single write-primary PostgreSQL cluster.
The existing application performs transactions across tenant-aware schemas.
The most recent full restore rehearsal is more than 12 months old.
Logical replication has not yet been demonstrated at the recorded peak write rate.
The approved first-year spending ceiling is 125 percent of current annual platform cost.
